## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:blocked`

> ⏳ **The AI reviewer could not run — this is NOT a review of your code.**
>
> Almost always the **Claude subscription session quota** is exhausted (also possible: rate-limit / overload). The required `ai-review` check is `action_required` — it blocks merge only because un-reviewed code must not land — and it **re-runs automatically** when the quota window resets (the `ai-review-retry` workflow).
>
> **Options:**
> 1. **Wait** for the quota window to reset — the retry workflow re-reviews automatically.
> 2. **Fail over to PAYG API** — set repo variable `AI_REVIEW_FAILOVER=payg` + secret `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; re-runs then use pay-as-you-go instead of the subscription quota.
> 3. Re-run the `ai-review` workflow manually once quota is back.

<details><summary>reviewer output (redacted — may include the reset time)</summary>

```
REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE_BEGIN
reason: quota
evidence: NONE (reason is inferred, not observed)
classified_via: stdout(strict)
stderr_bytes: 0
stdout_bytes: 25
detail: |
  (no diagnostic text on either stream — see #1630)
REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE_END
```
</details>

_Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]`. Transient/quota failures are surfaced as `ai-review:blocked` (distinct from `ai-review:changes`) so a token outage never masquerades as a code-review verdict._

### Update from the orphan-PR driver

Merged `origin/main` into `agent/issue-1106` as e21cd162. The merge was clean, and the net diff against `main` is unchanged: the same three files (`docs/decisions/DR-091.md`, `docs/decisions/INDEX.md`, `specs/minspec/SPEC-067-triage-dispute/requirements.md`). A fresh AI review is running on this head.

**I did not make the blocking change (renumber DR-091 to DR-090 and SPEC-067 to SPEC-066), because it would bring back a collision.**

- #1776 (managed-prose vantage, open, `ai-review:pass` + `awaiting-approval`) already adds both `docs/decisions/DR-090.md` and `specs/minspec/SPEC-066-managed-prose-vantage/`. This PR moved to the next free ids in 294bf116 and 0ab2e178, under the tie-break its description records (lowest PR number keeps the id).
- The repo's own `DR id uniqueness` gate (`.github/workflows/dr-id-collision.yml` running `scripts/check-dr-id-collision.ts`) checks ids across `main` **and every open PR**. On e21cd162 it printed `DR id check: DR-091 is free on main and across every open PR. (Next free id: DR-094.)` A renamed `DR-090` would duplicate #1776's record in that same check.
- The reviewers compute max + 1 against the base checkout only. They have no network or `gh` access, so they cannot see open PRs. That is the gap tracked in #1932 (ai-review blocks a correctly-reserved DR id), which names this PR. The SPEC half has no cross-PR gate at all yet: #1860 (the id gate is filename-keyed).

So the finding asks for a number that a merge-gating check would reject. The ids become in-sequence on the base as soon as #1776 merges. After that, one more `main` merge here gives the reviewers a base whose highest ids are DR-090 and SPEC-066, and DR-091 / SPEC-067 are then simply the next numbers.

**Non-blocking findings**

- *"Sub-issues #1788 to #1792 are unverifiable"*: I checked them on GitHub. All five exist, are open, and carry the stated labels: #1788 (`role:architect`, `needs-review`, `hold:human`), and #1789, #1790, #1791, #1792 (`role:dev`, `needs-review`).
- *Full URL for #1106 in the spec header*: not changed. It is a style nit inside the spec text, and this pass does not edit the spec.
- *`affects:` freeze on `dispatch-ready-check.sh` / `triage-inbox.sh`*: already disclosed in the spec's Context section. The founder decides this when advancing past Clarify.

➡️ **Founder: choose the merge order.** **(rec)** Merge #1776 first, then refresh this PR from `main` so its next review sees DR-090 / SPEC-066 on the base. Cost: this PR waits on #1776, and the refresh costs one more review-panel run. The alternative is to add a sentence to DR-091 and SPEC-067 recording the reservation, so the reviewers can see it in the diff. Cost: that edits the proposed record and spec, restarts review on them, and the sentence goes stale the moment #1776 lands. The lasting fix for both is #1932.

commits.messageBody:
Design-only output for #1106, the follow-up DR-072 §3 filed against itself.
DR-072 closed the hold-lifting question but answered the mis-classification
question in prose — "reword the issue body until the classifier agrees" — which
is undocumented, teaches unbounded prompt-gaming against a non-deterministic
classifier, and destroys the human/classifier disagreement that is the only
corpus able to say how often the human-only filter is wrong.

DR-090 records the lane; SPEC-066 carries the contract, file allowlists,
invariants and the four sub-issue definitions. The distinction the whole record
turns on: correcting an INPUT tells the gate what the work is and the gate then
decides; overriding an OUTPUT tells the gate what to conclude.

Five load-bearing properties:

- triage-decide.sh is NOT modified (SPEC-066 FR-12) — the deterministic gate's
  inputs stay the agent's five verdict fields.
- A declared type settles the TYPE leg of the human-only filter and hands the
  INTENT leg back to the classifier, so a dispute can FAIL on the record. That
  is what distinguishes it from an override.
- The dispute record uses its own sentinel family and OMITS decision/hold/
  human_only/role/tier, so a forged one authorises nothing. DR-072 §3's
  liftable-hold table gains no row; hold:human stays absolute.
- One loosening dispute per (issue, bodyHash) — the bound is on the body, not
  the declared type, so cycling type tokens is not a slower slot machine.
- Only the gate-validated enum reaches the classifier; the free-text reason is
  never passed, and fence_agent_text gains the new sentinel family.

DR-090 §8 names a kill criterion before the mechanism ships: at n>=20 loosening
disputes, an upheld rate >= 0.95 means the classifier is rubber-stamping and the
lane is withdrawn rather than tuned.

Artifacts: docs/decisions/DR-090.md (status: proposed, born-proposed per DR-029),
specs/minspec/SPEC-066-triage-dispute/requirements.md (T3, specify: done),
docs/decisions/INDEX.md entry.

No implementation code — packages/ and tests/ untouched, per the role allowlist.
The four sub-issues could not be filed (this agent holds no gh/network access per
DR-008); they are written out in full in SPEC-066 §Sub-issues (A)-(D).

npm test: 281 files / 5732 tests pass. npm run validate: passes.

commits.messageBody:
…te design

Root cause: INV-4's mint-time uniqueness bound had only one predicate to lean
on, C-3's `--fresh-dispute`, which answers a recency-scoped question (the
newest dispute at a bodyHash) — while FR-5's "at most one loosening dispute
per (issue, bodyHash)" needs a full-history existence question. A tightening
dispute minted afterward at the same hash becomes "the newest," so a
recency-only check silently stops seeing an earlier loosening dispute at all.

Root cause: FR-4's "fresh" (selectable for classifier injection) was keyed
only on bodyHash and trusted authorship, with no reference to whether a
verdict had already been minted since the dispute was filed. triage-inbox.sh
is an explicitly supported per-issue invocation and a re-triage never changes
the bodyHash, so nothing stopped a bare re-invocation against an unedited
body from re-injecting the same declaredType on every run — DR-090 §4's
minting bound closes re-*recording* a dispute but did nothing to close
re-*reading* the one already recorded.

Fixes, both design-only — SPEC-066 is still specify:done/clarify:pending, no
code exists yet:

- New C-3 entry point `--dispute-exists <bodyHash> <direction>`: a
  full-history existence scan, deliberately separate from `--fresh-dispute`,
  so FR-5's mint-time check can never be satisfied by "the newest one so
  far." `--fresh-dispute` gains a once-only consumption condition instead: a
  dispute is selectable only while its disputedVerdictAt still equals the
  current newest verdict's verdictAt. FR-4, FR-7, FR-11 and DR-090 §4 now
  describe the same mechanism; INV-4 names both predicates rather than
  asserting a property nothing checked.
- `--may-dispute`'s `human_only` parameter now has a stated meaning and
  precedence — checked first and independently, mirroring `--may-approve`
  (dispatch-ready-check.sh:468-472) — refusing a garbled hold/human_only
  pairing as `[garbled-record]` before `direction` is consulted.
- DR-090 §5's wire-form example now shows one concrete `direction` value;
  `loosening | tightening` is not a value record_scrub can carry.
- SPEC-066's frontmatter now discloses that its `affects:` declaration arms
  a repo-wide freeze on dispatch-ready-check.sh/triage-inbox.sh via
  spec-gate.py the moment this spec's phase passes Clarify while unapproved
  (verified against spec-gate.py:285,349-350,368,487-488).
- Filed the four SPEC-066 sub-issues (#1789-#1792) and the DR-090
  type-inference follow-up (#1788) that the authoring agent could not file
  (no gh/network access, DR-008). Labelled `needs-review` rather than the
  spec's own `agent-ready`, since SPEC-066 and DR-090 are both still
  unapproved as of filing.
- Deleted two untracked scratch files (.commit-msg.txt, .regen-dr-index.ts)
  left in the worktree. Verified the INDEX.md DR-090 entry's fingerprint
  (auto=c5ac0ec77f33) against the real buildDrIndexContent()/renderDrEntry()
  output via tsx — it matches exactly, so no regen was needed.

Artifacts: docs/decisions/DR-090.md, specs/minspec/SPEC-066-triage-dispute/requirements.md.
No implementation code touched; no status:/phases: frontmatter changed.

npm run validate: passes (142 non-fatal warnings, all pre-existing; the 2 for
SPEC-066 are its expected missing design.md/tasks.md, unrelated to this change).

commits.messageBody:
Three open PRs each independently minted a NEW decision record declaring
`id: DR-090`: #1776 ("Prose inside a managed file is shipped code"), this PR
(#1783, "A wrong triage classification is a corrected INPUT"), and #1835
("A harness refresh may only move a project forward"). `nextAdrNumber` hands
out max(existing) + 1 computed against the LOCAL checkout, which is unique only
if DR creation is serialised through main. Concurrent worktree sessions break
that by design, and all three branched from a main whose highest id was DR-089.

Tie-break: the lowest PR number keeps the id, so #1776 retains DR-090. This PR
takes the first free id and #1835 takes the second.

DR-091 is free: origin/main holds DR-001..DR-089 with no gaps (89 files), and
of every open PR only #1776, #1783 and #1835 add a docs/decisions/DR-NNN.md,
all three claiming DR-090. Nothing open claims DR-091 or above.

Identifier only. The decision's content, argument and `status: proposed` are
untouched: the DR file changes exactly two lines (frontmatter `id:` and the
title heading), and all 27 changed lines in the spec differ only by the id.
INDEX.md was regenerated with the repo's own generator (`regenerateDrIndex`)
rather than hand-edited, since it is a marker-managed file; its `auto=` summary
hash is unchanged, confirming the summarised content did not move.

The 089 to 091 gap on this branch is expected and closes when #1776 lands
DR-090. `validateDrSequence` reports a gap as a warning, not a failure; the
FATAL rule (duplicate id / id-filename mismatch) passes clean over all 90 files.
